comparator.title: Energy gel comparator
comparator.subtitle: Interactive table with verified nutrition data and cost per gram of carbohydrate.
comparator.disclaimer: Reference prices with verification date. PedalSci earns a commission on purchases made through the links in this table, at no extra cost to you.
comparator.methodologyText: Nutrition data is manually verified against each manufacturer's official product pages. Cost per gram of carbohydrate is calculated by dividing the gel's retail price by the grams of carbohydrate per serving.

evidence.title: Supplement evidence explorer
evidence.subtitle: What the science says about 19 supplements for cycling and endurance, on a dual axis: how solid the evidence is and which way the effect points.
evidence.legendAxisLevel: Evidence level — how solid the research is.
evidence.legendAxisDirection: Direction — which way the effect points.
evidence.legendNote: Important: “strong” means the evidence is robust, not that the effect is large. And “against” means the evidence shows it does not work or that it harms — not that research is missing.
evidence.methodologyText: Each supplement is rated on a dual-axis model: the evidence level (how solid the research is) is kept separate from the effect direction (whether it helps, does nothing, or harms). A “strong” level means robustness, not a large effect. All 123 citations were verified one by one against PubMed, and extrapolations (from other sports or from one sex to the other) are stated explicitly. WADA and AIS statuses were checked against official sources.
evidence.disclaimer: Educational information, not medical or nutritional advice. Consult a professional before supplementing, especially if you compete under anti-doping rules.

levelDesc.fuerte: Solid, consistent evidence (several RCTs or meta-analyses). High robustness, not necessarily a large effect.
levelDesc.moderada: Reasonable evidence but with heterogeneity or gaps. Effect likely.
levelDesc.limitada: Sparse, preliminary or indirect evidence. Uncertain.
levelDesc.en_contra: Evidence shows it does not work or that it harms. Not “lack of studies”.

directionDesc.contextual: Only helps in a specific context (heat, deficiency, repeated sprints…).
directionDesc.perjudicial: May impair performance or training adaptations.

climbs.title: World climbs database
climbs.subtitle: Iconic cycling climbs with their FIETS difficulty index and an elevation profile computed from the digital elevation model.
climbs.fietsExplain: The FIETS index summarises difficulty by combining elevation gain, length and summit altitude. The higher the value, the harder the climb.
climbs.profileDemNote: Profile sampled from the SRTM 30 m DEM along the real road geometry.
climbs.profileSyntheticNote: Profile reconstructed from the curated length and gain (approximate, not sampled on the ground).
climbs.legendNote: Difficulty bands are derived from the FIETS index, a public, reproducible formula computed from our curated figures.

difficultyDesc.mitica: The hardest on the planet, FIETS ≥ 9.

climbs.methodologyText: Figures (length, gain, gradient and altitude) are verified by hand against specialist sources (Climbfinder, PJAMM Cycling, cyclingcols, Wikipedia), cited per climb. The elevation profile is computed by sampling the open SRTM 30 m digital elevation model (Open Topo Data) along the real road geometry (routed with BRouter); where routing or the DEM was unavailable, the profile is reconstructed from the curated figures and flagged as synthetic.
climbs.disclaimer: Data provided for ride-planning information only. Always check road condition, seasonal closures and traffic before riding.

races.title: 2026 UCI calendar
races.subtitle: The international road-cycling calendar: WorldTour, ProSeries and selected continental races, men's and women's.
races.methodologyText: Calendar curated and verified by hand from public sources (ProCyclingStats, UCI and each race's official site), cited per row. Factual data —name, date, country and UCI class— is not copyrightable; it is re-expressed, not copied as tables. Only races whose 2026 date could be verified are included.
races.disclaimer: Dates and categories are subject to change by the UCI and organisers. Always check each race's official site before planning.

about.intro: A digital cycling publication that combines artificial intelligence with real scientific sources. Every article is researched and drafted with the help of AI, then edited and reviewed with journalistic rigor before it is published.
about.whatWeDoP1: PedalSci is built on a premise: cycling deserves science-based journalism grounded in evidence. No opinions disguised as science, no sensationalist headlines. Data, studies and verifiable sources.
about.whatWeDoP2: To get there, we use artificial intelligence as a research and writing tool. Every article starts from real scientific sources — studies from PubMed, Semantic Scholar and peer-reviewed journals. AI speeds up the process; editorial judgment decides what gets published and how.
about.whatWeDoP3: Before publication, every article goes through editorial review. Sources are cited explicitly so any reader can verify the information on their own.
about.editorialProcessIntro: PedalSci is produced with an editorial process that is AI-assisted and supervised by people at every stage.
about.step1Text: The editorial team decides what is worth covering and from which angle, prioritizing what genuinely helps the cyclist.
about.step2Text: Every article starts from peer-reviewed literature — studies from PubMed, Semantic Scholar and specialized journals — not a generic web summary.
about.step3Title: We draft with the help of AI
about.step3Text: We use artificial intelligence as a tool to draft from those sources. It speeds up the first draft; it does not decide what is true or what gets published.
about.step4Text: Before publishing, the editorial team reviews the text, checks that every claim matches the cited sources and corrects whatever is needed.
about.step5Text: We publish with sources cited explicitly so anyone can verify them. If you spot an error, we fix it.
about.ourTeamIntro: The people who research, write, edit and fact-check every article. AI is our working tool; the editorial judgement is always human.
about.transparencyText: PedalSci is produced with an AI-assisted process supervised by our editorial team. AI helps research and draft from real scientific sources; the decision of what gets published, the fact-checking and the final edit are the responsibility of people. The names for each section are the editorial bylines we publish each specialty under.
